title: Splitwise expense sharing design
idea: A Splitwise design records who paid and who shared each expense, keeps one net balance per person, and turns those balances into a short list of payments.

analogy.text: A notebook on a shared flat's fridge. Each purchase is one line; at month end you total everyone's column and settle up.
analogy.breaks: A notebook cannot reject shares that do not add up.

points: Each split rule is a strategy with one method: `shares(total, users)`.
Money is stored in whole cents, so leftover cents are assigned on purpose.
The ledger keeps one net number per person, not a pile of pairwise debts.
Settling matches the largest debtor with the largest creditor until everyone is even.

edges.label: shares?
edges.caption: The expense asks its strategy for each person's share. The ledger never knows which rule was used.

edges.label: throws
edges.caption: An exact split that does not add up throws before any balance changes.

edges.label: shares
edges.caption: Each sharer's balance goes down by their share; the payer's goes up by the same amount.

edges.label: net balances
edges.caption: Balances always sum to zero. Positive means owed money, negative means owing.

edges.label: transfers
edges.caption: Each match zeroes at least one person, so payments never exceed people minus one.

code.title: Split strategies and ledger
code.caption: Add a `PercentSplit` class with the same `shares` method. The `Ledger` needs no change.

walk.text: Equal split hands leftover cents to the first users, so shares always sum to the total.
Exact split validates that the given amounts add up, or throws.
Shares are computed first, so a bad split leaves balances untouched.
Every share moves money from the sharer's balance to the payer's.
Two good expenses, one rejected, then the net balances.

code.title: Simplify the debts
code.caption: Balances in, payments out. Change the numbers, keeping their sum at zero, and rerun.

walk.text: Copy balances into objects we can update.
Sort so the biggest debtor is first and the biggest creditor last; stop when either is even.
Pay the smaller of the two amounts, which zeroes at least one of them.

pitfalls: Never store money as floating-point; use integer cents and assign leftovers explicitly.
Validate the split before updating any balance, or a failure leaves half-applied state.
Do not add a new `if` per split type; add a strategy class instead.

quiz.why: `base` is 33 and one cent is left over. The index check gives it to the first user.

takeaway: Strategies compute shares, the ledger nets them, and settle pays them off.

starters: How would I support groups and per-group balances?
Is the greedy settle always the minimum number of payments?
How would I add a percentage split without rounding errors?
